sugestoes.texto: An attacker-controlled Referer containing a quote breaks out of the single-quoted JS string and executes script in the Discourse origin. Serialize `request.referer` with `to_json` instead of interpolating it unescaped.

A crafted URL with quotes or markup persists and executes when rendered via `post.cooked` in the embed view. Escape `url` with `ERB::Util.html_escape` before interpolating it into HTML saved with the `raw_html` cook method.
The exception aborts `poll_feed` and drops all remaining items in the feed. Coerce `i.content` with `to_s` before calling `scrub` to handle items without content and avoid `NoMethodError`.
A slow or huge embed URL hangs the job worker and starves the queue. Read `url` via `URI.open` with `open_timeout`, `read_timeout`, and a `read` size limit instead of unbounded `open`.
A crash between the commands leaves a key with no TTL that suppresses future retrieves forever. Set `retrieved_key` atomically with `set` using `nx` and `ex` instead of separate `setnx` and `expire`.

The loser raises `RecordNotUnique` and aborts the retrieve/poll job instead of reusing the winner's row. Wrap the `embed.blank?` and `create!` check-then-create on `embed_url` to catch `RecordNotUnique` and reuse the winner's row.

Distinct embed URLs bypass the per-URL throttle and fan one lightweight miss out into feed-scale network plus database work. Return early on `TopicEmbed` existence for `embed_url` instead of running `Jobs::PollFeed` synchronously with `execute`.

issues.descricao: The postMessage handler in embed.js checks the sender with discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin), a substring test instead of exact origin equality, so a page on an origin that is a substring of the Discourse URL can send forged discourse-resize messages to the embedding page.
issues.textoGolden: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.

comentarios.texto: The message-origin check uses substring matching: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`. Any origin that is a substring of discourseUrl is accepted (e.g. discourseUrl `https://discourse.example.com` accepts origin `https://discourse`), so a malicious page can post `discourse-resize` messages into the embed. Compare against the iframe's actual origin exactly (`e.origin !== expectedOrigin`) instead of a substring test.
Uses indexOf containment instead of origin equality, but it cannot be bypassed.

WHAT: postMessage origin check is reversed (`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin)===-1`) instead of strict origin equality. WHY: any e.origin that is a substring of discourseUrl passes, letting a foreign iframe drive `iframe.height` handling and future message branches.

issues.descricao: The referer and embed_url host checks compare against SiteSetting.embeddable_host case-sensitively, so a host differing only in case is rejected even though hostnames are case-insensitive.

comentarios.texto: Host identity is compared case-sensitively: `URI(request.referer).host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. Hostnames are case-insensitive, so a referer such as `http://EVILTROUT.COM/...` never matches the configured `eviltrout.com` (and the same flaw exists in lib/topic_retriever.rb:15 for `URI(@embed_url).host`). Normalize both sides with downcase before comparing so case variations of the same host are treated identically.

The referer/host comparison does not lowercase either side, so a mixed-case host is wrongly rejected. The reviewer notes this fails closed and is not a bypass. Normalize case on both sides of the host comparison (e.g. downcase both) to avoid false rejections. The same issue applies to topic_retriever.rb.

The host comparison does not lowercase either side, so a mixed-case host is wrongly rejected. This fails closed and is not a bypass. Normalize case on both sides of the comparison (e.g. downcase both) to avoid false rejections.

issues.descricao: PollFeed reads i.content.scrub for every feed item, so items without a content element (common in RSS feeds that only have description) raise NoMethodError and abort the import of the remaining items.
issues.textoGolden: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` assumes every feed item has a `content` element. WHY: many RSS 2.0 items expose only `<description>` (simple-rss returns nil for `content`), so `nil.scrub` raises NoMethodError and, because the job is `sidekiq_options retry: false`, the entire hourly feed import for all items is aborted. HOW: fall back to the available field, e.g. `(i.content || i.description || i.summary).to_s.scrub`, and skip items whose body is blank.

The feed item is consumed unconditionally: url = i.link, then i.title, and content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub). SimpleRSS item accessors raise NoMethodError when the element is absent (RSS 2.0 feeds frequently carry only <description>, no <content>, and some items have no <link>/<title>), so a single malformed or content-less item aborts the whole hourly job with an unhandled exception instead of skipping it. The code already anticipates a blank link (line 33 fallback) but reads i.content/i.title without a nil guard; use i.content.to_s (or fall back to i.description/summary) and skip items whose content is blank.

`i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError when a feed item has no content (only a description). The exception aborts the whole poll, so every item after it is never imported. Fall back to `i.content || i.description`, skip items with blank content, and rescue per item.

issues.descricao: Posts imported from RSS or remote pages use cook_method raw_html, which makes Post#cook return the raw HTML without sanitization, and the embed view outputs it with raw post.cooked, allowing stored XSS from imported content.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: the new `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` makes `Post#cook` return completely unsanitized HTML, and Jobs::PollFeed stores untrusted feed content this way (poll_feed.rb:35-36 → TopicEmbed.import, unlike import_remote which sanitizes via Readability's tag/attribute whitelist). WHY: the stored `cooked` value is then emitted with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19, and that page is served from the forum's own origin — so a malicious/compromised RSS feed item containing `<script>` or `onerror=` runs attacker JavaScript in the forum origin and can read cookies/session and perform authenticated actions (stored XSS). HOW: sanitize the raw HTML before persisting it (e.g. run the feed content through the same HTML sanitizer used for regular posts, or restrict the raw_html cook path to trusted, pre-sanitized sources only).

WHAT: Post#cook returns raw verbatim for cook_method raw_html, skipping the cooking/sanitization pipeline and plugin filters. WHY: any RSS/readability HTML imported via TopicEmbed is rendered unsanitized in embed/best.html.erb, executing attacker script in the Discourse origin.

Feed-provided HTML is persisted with raw_html cooking after only Nokogiri parsing and URL rewriting, which do not sanitize scripts or event-handler attributes. A malicious feed entry containing executable HTML is stored as post.cooked and executed under the forum origin when rendered, including through the new raw cooked embed view. Sanitize imported HTML with an explicit safe tag, attribute and URL-scheme allowlist before storing it or returning it from the raw_html cooking path.

issues.descricao: TopicEmbed.import appends a footer that interpolates the URL unescaped into an <a href='...'> tag in raw HTML that is later rendered unsanitized, so a crafted URL can inject markup; it also appends to contents with << without handling nil.
issues.textoGolden: The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: TopicEmbed.import interpolates feed-controlled url unescaped into raw HTML (`#{url}`) and stores feed HTML as raw_html. WHY: url passing /^https?\:\/\// can still contain `'`, `>` or script, and RSS content is never sanitized, giving stored XSS when rendered via `raw post.cooked`. HOW: HTML-escape url and sanitize content instead of raw_html passthrough.

TopicEmbed.import interpolates feed-controlled url unescaped into HTML link stored with cook_method raw_html (Post#cook returns raw, bypassing pipeline) and rendered with raw post.cooked: XSS via quote/script break-out. Escape url for text and attribute contexts before storing.

The url is interpolated unescaped into `#{url}`. The post is stored with cook_method raw_html and rendered with `raw post.cooked`, so a url containing a quote or markup is output as live HTML. Escape it with ERB::Util.html_escape (or CGI.escapeHTML) for both the href and the link text.

issues.descricao: TopicEmbed.import appends the footer with contents <<, mutating the caller's string in place instead of building a new string.

comentarios.texto: `contents <<` mutates the caller's string in place. This raises FrozenError for frozen strings and appends the footer twice if the same string is imported again. Use `contents = contents + ...` instead.

issues.descricao: TopicEmbed.import checks for an existing embed and then creates the post and TopicEmbed without handling the unique-index conflict, so two concurrent imports of the same URL make one job fail with RecordNotUnique.

comentarios.texto: TopicEmbed.import does a check-then-insert on embed_url (where(...).first, then TopicEmbed.create!) with no rescue for the unique index declared on topic_embeds.embed_url. The only guard against concurrent intake is the Redis throttle in TopicRetriever, which is bypassed for staff (retrieve_topic.rb:17 passes no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)) and can expire while a slow retrieval (which may synchronously run a full PollFeed, topic_retriever.rb:41) is still running. Two interleaved retrievals for the same URL both see embed.blank? and both attempt creation; the loser raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique, which is unhandled anywhere in the job path, breaking execution. Guard the create against the race (rescue/retry on RecordNotUnique, or use find_or_create_by on embed_url inside the transaction) so concurrent retrievals cannot raise.

Make creation idempotent under concurrent imports. Two workers can both read no embed at line 15 and create posts before attempting the same unique embed_url insert. The unique index correctly rolls back the losing transaction, but its unhandled uniqueness exception aborts that job (and potentially the rest of a feed polling run). This is reachable when scheduled polling overlaps retrieval-triggered polling; the per-URL retrieval throttle does not serialize those paths. Handle the conflict outside the transaction and return the winning embed/post, or serialize imports for the URL.

Race on check-then-create: two concurrent imports both see TopicEmbed.where(embed_url:url).first blank, both create Post + TopicEmbed.create!. Unique index on embed_url then raises RecordNotUnique (unhandled) or creates duplicates. Need atomic find-or-create / rescue unique violation.

issues.descricao: When the embedded post has been deleted, TopicEmbed.import's update path passes a nil embed.post to PostRevisor and crashes on every later import of that URL.

comentarios.texto: On the update path `embed.post` can be nil if the post was deleted. `PostRevisor.new(nil)` then raises NoMethodError, and every later import of that URL fails the same way. Guard against a nil post, for example by skipping the revision or recreating the topic.

WHAT: update path uses `embed.post` without nil guard then `PostRevisor.new(post)`. WHY: if the first post was deleted, post is nil and revise! dereferences nil, crashing feed-poll updates instead of recreating/skipping.

Orphan-post crash on update path: post = embed.post can be nil if the post/topic was deleted, then PostRevisor.new(nil).revise! raises NoMethodError. Must handle missing post (recreate or skip) instead of assuming present.

issues.descricao: Claims import_remote crashes on unparseable pages (nil content) and dead URLs because it does no nil check or network error handling around open(url).read.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: import_remote passes `doc.content` (and title) directly to import where `contents <<` assumes a String, with no nil check or network-error handling around `open(url).read`. WHY: unparseable pages (nil content) raise NoMethodError and dead URLs raise OpenURI errors, crashing RetrieveTopic/Disqus imports with no topic created.

issues.descricao: absolutize_urls only handles root-relative paths: protocol-relative URLs like //cdn.example.com/x.png are rewritten to http://host/cdn.example.com/x.png and path-relative links are left unresolved, breaking links and images in imported posts.

comentarios.texto: The URL rewrite treats protocol-relative URLs such as `//cdn.example.com/image.jpg` as paths on the article host, producing `http://article-host/cdn.example.com/image.jpg`. Imported images and links using protocol-relative external URLs therefore point to the wrong server. Resolve both href and src using URI joining against the article URL, which also handles ordinary relative paths correctly.

Resolve relative href/src references with URI joining rather than handling only leading slashes. For an article at http://example.com/blog/article, href='next' and src='images/photo.jpg' remain relative and resolve against the forum instead of the imported article. Moreover, '//cdn.example.com/photo.jpg' is rewritten to 'http://example.com/cdn.example.com/photo.jpg'. Both yield incorrect links/images in imported posts; apply proper URI resolution to both anchors and images.

absolutize_urls treats any href or src starting with '/' as site-relative and strips all leading slashes. Protocol-relative URLs like '//cdn.example.com/a.png' are rewritten to 'http://site/cdn.example.com/a.png', which is broken. Skip values starting with '//' (or prefix them with the scheme) and only rewrite single-slash paths.

issues.descricao: The embed view formats post dates with a hard-coded strftime pattern, so users in non-English locales see English month names and a fixed order while the rest of the view is translated.

comentarios.texto: The post date uses a hard-coded strftime format `"%e %b %Y"`. `%b` emits English month abbreviations (Jan, Feb, ...) no matter what locale the viewer is in, so the date is frozen to en-US while the surrounding strings in this same view are localized via I18n.t. This is a locale-pinned user-facing format; it should be localized (e.g. via the app's localized date helper / l( ) rather than a literal strftime pattern).

Use a localized date formatter rather than strftime("%e %b %Y"). %b produces English month abbreviations and the fixed day-month-year order ignores the selected locale, although the neighbouring header and footer labels are translated. Embedded comments therefore show English-formatted dates for users of other locales.
Date uses strftime("%e %b %Y") hard-coding one locale's month names/order while neighbouring strings go through I18n.t. Use I18n.l with a locale date format so non-English users see localized dates.

issues.descricao: The Disqus importer now creates topics through TopicEmbed.import_remote, dropping the thread's created_at and the category option and requiring a live HTTP fetch per thread, so imported topics get wrong dates/categories and a dead link aborts the import.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: Disqus import replaced PostCreator (title/raw/created_at/category) with `TopicEmbed.import_remote` per thread, dropping category_id, created_at, and strip handling. WHY: imported topics lose categories/timestamps and now require a live HTTP fetch per thread, failing when links are dead.

Preserve the Disqus thread creation timestamp when switching to TopicEmbed.import_remote. The previous PostCreator call passed `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])`, but this replacement passes only the title, and TopicEmbed.import_remote/import never forward a timestamp to PostCreator. Imported historical topics now get the migration time as their initial post creation date while their replies retain historical dates, losing the importer's chronological fidelity. Extend the import options to forward created_at and pass the thread timestamp here.

The Disqus import now calls TopicEmbed.import_remote instead of PostCreator. This silently drops the `--category` option and the `created_at` from the Disqus thread, and the `--category` method_option was removed from the CLI. It also now makes a live HTTP fetch of every thread link, and `open(url)` raises on a failure that previously could not happen, aborting the whole import. Keep the category and date handling, and rescue fetch errors per thread.

issues.descricao: Every retrieval of an article not yet embedded synchronously polls and imports the entire RSS feed, and since throttling is per URL, many different article requests repeat the full feed download and processing.

comentarios.texto: Every uncached article retrieval synchronously downloads and processes the complete configured feed before fetching the article. Because the retrieval throttle is keyed by individual embed URL, simultaneous requests for different articles each repeat the feed download and all per-item database lookups/imports, multiplying worker load by the number of requests times feed size. Coalesce feed polling with a feed-wide throttle or lock and reuse its recent results instead of executing a full poll per article.

issues.descricao: The 'is 404 without an embed_url' spec never sets an embeddable host, so the request is rejected by ensure_embeddable before the embed_url check runs, and the test would pass even without that check.

comentarios.texto: The test is named 'is 404 without an embed_url' but passes for the wrong reason: it never sets embeddable_host, which defaults to '' so the before_filter `ensure_embeddable` raises at the blank-host check before `params.require(:embed_url)` is reached. The request is rejected regardless of whether the embed_url requirement exists, so the test would still pass if that requirement were removed. Stub a valid embeddable_host here so the failure is actually attributable to the missing embed_url.

The missing-embed_url test does not establish a valid embeddable host and referer, so ensure_embeddable rejects this request before best reaches params.require(:embed_url). It also only checks non-success despite claiming a 404. Removing the required-parameter check would therefore leave this test green. Configure an allowed host/referer for this case and assert the intended missing-parameter response.

The 'is 404 without an embed_url' test never sets embeddable_host, so ensure_embeddable rejects the request before params.require(:embed_url) runs. It passes without the embed_url check. Stub embeddable_host and the referer so the missing param is the only failure cause.

issues.descricao: The 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' specs leave feed_polling_enabled at its false default, so they never reach the condition they name and would pass with those checks deleted.

comentarios.texto: The three 'requires ...' tests do not isolate the guard they name: each stubs only one setting to falsy while the other two remain falsy by default, so poll_feed is never called even if the named check were deleted. Stub the other two settings to truthy values in each test so removing the named guard would cause poll_feed to run and fail the test.

These two tests do not verify the conditions they name. `execute` is guarded by `feed_polling_enabled? && feed_polling_url.present? && embed_by_username.present?`, and feed_polling_enabled defaults to false. Neither test stubs feed_polling_enabled? to true, so the guard short-circuits at the first clause and poll_feed is never called no matter what feed_polling_url/embed_by_username are. Both would still pass if the URL/username checks were deleted entirely. Stub `SiteSetting.stubs(:feed_polling_enabled?).returns(true)` in each so the specific condition under test is actually reached.

The URL and username prerequisite tests never enable feed polling (whose configured default is false) or supply the other required setting. execute consequently short-circuits at feed_polling_enabled? and never evaluates the prerequisite each test claims to cover. Both tests still pass if their corresponding presence checks are removed. Set all other prerequisites to valid values before making only the setting under test absent, so the poll_feed.never expectation actually detects removal of that guard.

issues.descricao: PollFeed.feed_key computes a per-feed cache key that is never used, so the feed is re-fetched and re-processed every hour without a modified-since check.
The embed layout references the 'embed' stylesheet and embed.js, but neither is in config.assets.precompile, so with precompiled assets in production the embed page fails to load them.
The retrieve throttle is keyed by the full embed URL, so an anonymous client can vary the query string on the embeddable host to bypass it and make the server create an unbounded number of topics.

The "requires feed_polling_enabled?" spec leaves feed_polling_url and embed_by_username at their blank defaults, so poll_feed is skipped regardless and the test would pass even without the enabled check.

sugestoes.texto: A host containing a quote breaks the migration and enables SQL injection from stored setting values. Quote `h` with `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote` or use parameterized exec in the `INSERT`.
Fresh installs without `embed_category` settings hit `NoMethodError` on `nil`. Guard the `[0]['id']` / `['value']` lookups and fall back to uncategorized or skip when empty.
A null or non-array id list throws `TypeError` during hydration of any rest-serialized payload. Guard `obj[k]` with an array check and default to an empty array before calling `map`.

A configured host like `example.com:8080` never matches its own referer, so embedding silently fails for port hosts. Include the non-default `uri.port` with downcasing in `record_for_host` or strip ports on save.
Creating a record with a blank host crashes with `NoMethodError` instead of failing validation. Return early in `before_validation` unless `self.host` is present before calling `sub!`.
Model types with multiple underscores never match `ADMIN_MODELS` and get the wrong base path. Change `type.replace('_', '-')` to use `/_/g` so all underscores are replaced.

issues.descricao: EmbeddableHost's before_validation calls self.host.sub! unconditionally, so saving a record with a nil host raises NoMethodError instead of returning a validation error.
issues.textoGolden: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

comentarios.texto: The before_validation callback calls `sub!` on host without guarding nil. Creating a host with a missing or null host field reaches this callback from save_host and raises NoMethodError instead of returning a validation error. Guard nil during normalization and let presence/format validation reject it.

WHAT: `before_validation` calls `self.host.sub!(...)` unconditionally, so a record with a nil host raises NoMethodError (`nil.sub!`) instead of producing a normal format-invalid result. WHY: `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` assigns `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` directly; any request that omits the host value makes the save raise a 500 instead of returning the `render_json_error(host)` validation response. HOW: guard the mutation, e.g. `return if host.blank?` at the top of the before_validation block (or use `self.host = self.host.to_s` before stripping).

before_validation calls self.host.sub!(...) on a possibly-nil host before validates_format_of runs. The controller assigns host.host = params[:embeddable_host][:host], so a request without a host key leaves it nil and nil.sub! raises NoMethodError at save time instead of the format validation producing a normal error response. Add a presence guard so validation reports the failure.

issues.descricao: update and destroy in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController fetch the host with where(id:).first and never check for nil, so an unknown id raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of not-found.
issues.textoGolden: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.

comentarios.texto: In the destroy action, the nil-host case (line 15-16) would raise NoMethodError. Consider adding a nil check to handle the case where the host is not found.

update and destroy fetch the record with EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first but never check for nil, then immediately use it (save_host(host) does host.host = ... / host.save; destroy does host.destroy). A stale or already-deleted id, or an interleaving where a concurrent delete removes the row first, makes host nil and the first call on it raises NoMethodError -> unhandled 500. Guard with a nil/404 check before use.

Update passes the nullable result of where(...).first directly to save_host, which immediately assigns host.host. Updating a nonexistent or concurrently deleted record returns an internal error instead of a not-found response; destroy has the same lookup failure. Use find or explicitly raise a not-found error before dereferencing the lookup result.

issues.descricao: record_for_host compares lower(host) against the un-lowercased URI host, so mixed-case referer hosts fail to match allowed hosts and embedding is rejected.
issues.textoGolden: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

comentarios.texto: Normalize the parsed hostname before comparing it with lower(host). URI parsing preserves hostname case, so an allowed entry such as example.com does not match https://EXAMPLE.com/page even though DNS hostnames are case-insensitive. This makes valid embedding requests fail the host authorization check and makes category lookup inconsistent for equivalent domain identities. Compare against host.downcase (or normalize both operands equivalently), and add a mixed-case URL test.

The query compares lower(host) to the un-downcased uri.host. A referer such as http://EvilTrout.com never matches the stored lowercase host, so embedding is wrongly denied. Fix: use where("lower(host) = ?", host.downcase).

The query compares lower(host) in the database with uri.host, which is not lowercased, so the comparison normalizes only one side. A referer or URL with uppercase letters (e.g. http://EvilTrout.com) will not match the stored host. Compare against host.downcase, i.e. where('lower(host) = ?', host.downcase).

issues.descricao: The migration copies the legacy embeddable_hosts values into the new table without stripping scheme and path, so hosts stored as http://example.com no longer match the bare-host lookup and previously allowed embeds are rejected after upgrade.
issues.textoGolden: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: migration inserts raw embeddable_hosts lines (e.g. http://example.com/123) without stripping scheme/path like the model does. WHY: migrated rows never match EmbeddableHost.record_for_host which compares bare uri.host, silently breaking previously allowed embeds.

Migration INSERTs raw embeddable_hosts lines with scheme/path intact, but EmbeddableHost normalizes to bare domain (before_validation strips protocol/path, record_for_host looks up by URI.host). Strip protocol and path before INSERT or migrated hosts will never satisfy host_allowed?.

Legacy hosts are inserted verbatim instead of applying the new model's scheme/path normalization. Existing values such as http://discourse.org or https://example.com/1234 remain in the table, while record_for_host compares only URI.host, so previously configured embedding hosts stop working after upgrade. Normalize migrated entries to the same representation used by the model before inserting them.

issues.descricao: The contents of category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb are swapped, so each file defines the other's fabricators.
issues.textoGolden: The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

comentarios.texto: File named category_fabricator.rb now defines Fabricator(:embeddable_host) while Fabricator(:category) was moved to embeddable_host_fabricator.rb. Filenames disagree with contents — swap contents back so each file defines the fabricator its name states.

The file names and contents are swapped. embeddable_host_fabricator.rb defines the category fabricators (:category, :diff_category, :happy_category, :private_category), and category_fabricator.rb defines :embeddable_host. Restore category_fabricator.rb to the original category fabricators and put the :embeddable_host fabricator in embeddable_host_fabricator.rb.

issues.descricao: The migration builds its INSERT by interpolating each legacy host value into the SQL string instead of quoting or binding it, so a value with a quote breaks the statement.
issues.textoGolden: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

comentarios.texto: The migration's INSERT statement uses string interpolation: VALUES ('#{h}', ...). This is a SQL-injection concern and should be fixed by using parameterized queries or proper escaping.
WHAT: migration interpolates raw host string into SQL: VALUES ('#{h}', ...). WHY: a host value containing a single quote breaks the statement and allows SQL injection via site_settings value.

issues.descricao: The migration reads execute(...)[0]['id'] for embed_category without checking for an empty result, so installs without that setting stored crash the migration instead of falling back to the uncategorized category.
issues.textoGolden: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: migration does execute(...)[0]['id'] with no guard when embed_category setting/category is missing. WHY: nil[0] dereference crashes the migration and blocks deploy on instances without that setting.
Migration does execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking empty result; missing site_settings row throws NoMethodError and fails migration. Check for nil row.

The migration indexes the first category-query result before checking whether any row was returned. An installation without a persisted embed_category setting, or with no matching category name, aborts migration before reaching the uncategorized fallback. Check whether the result contains a row before accessing its id and handle missing fallback settings as well.

issues.descricao: The spec 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' no longer sets up any host condition and passes only because embed_truncate defaults to false, so its name no longer matches what it tests.

comentarios.texto: Test 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' does not establish the true-branch preconditions (embed_truncate true, has_topic_embed true) nor control host presence, so it passes regardless of host logic and would still pass if host checking were broken/removed. Set truncate true + stub embed true with no hosts for the false case.

The test named "is false if embeddable_host is blank" now uses an ordinary built topic without setting embed_truncate or making has_topic_embed? true. It therefore returns false for reasons unrelated to the missing host, and passes even with the new implementation that never checks host availability. If blank-host behavior remains the intended contract, arrange all the other prerequisites before asserting false; if the contract intentionally changed, replace this case with a test of the actual intended behavior rather than retaining a misleading passing test.

The description "is false if embeddable_host is blank" no longer matches the code. This PR changed Topic#expandable_first_post? (app/models/topic.rb:869) to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`, removing the embeddable_hosts condition entirely, and removed the `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts` setup from this test. The assertion now passes only because `has_topic_embed?` is unstubbed (false) and embed_truncate is unset, so the name states a cause the method no longer has — rename it (e.g. "is false when there is no topic embed") or set up the precondition it claims to test.

issues.descricao: The 'find embedded' test requests fruit 2 but the pretender always returns fruit 1, so it asserts fruit 1's colors and would not notice a find that ignores the id.

comentarios.texto: Test requests fruit id 2 but pretender returns fruits[0] unconditionally, so assertions on colors [1,2] never cover fruit 2's color_ids [3]. Make pretender honor :id or request id 1 / assert single-element case to actually verify plural _ids hydration.

This test now requests fruit 2 but expects fruit 1's two colors. The /fruits/:id Pretender handler always returns fruits[0], so the test passes while hydrating the wrong record and would not catch a find implementation that ignores the requested ID. Make the handler select the requested fruit and assert its ID and corresponding colors (fruit 2 has only color 3), or request fruit 1 if testing its two-color hydration is the goal.

issues.descricao: After saving a host, the component overwrites its category with findById(categoryId); when no category was chosen this is null even though the server saved the uncategorized category, so the row shows no category until reload.

comentarios.texto: The save callback overwrites the category using categoryId even when the server substituted the uncategorized category for a blank selection. Adding a host without choosing a category therefore leaves its category badge empty, and editing it reads an undefined category id despite a valid category_id having been returned. Resolve the category from the saved response's category_id rather than the submitted selection.

When categoryId is null (the default for a new row, or a cleared selection), the controller saves SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id and returns that category_id. This callback instead overwrites host.category with findById(null), making the displayed category disagree with the saved category. Use the category from the save response or its returned category_id rather than the pre-save selection.

Use the saved response's category rather than overwriting it from categoryId after saving. For a new host with no category selected, categoryId is null, while the new controller deliberately saves SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id and returns that ID through the serializer. This callback replaces the hydrated category with findById(null), leaving the row without its actual category until reload (and reopening edit also initializes from that incorrect relationship).

issues.descricao: Hosts saved with a port (allowed by the validation regex) are stored as host:port, but lookup compares only URI.host, so those configured hosts never match and embedding fails for them.

comentarios.texto: Host lookup compares URI.host against a stored value that validation explicitly permits to include a port. Saving example.com:8080 succeeds, but a request from http://example.com:8080 produces URI.host equal to example.com and never matches that record, disabling embedding and retrieval for the configured host. Use a consistent port representation in both storage and lookup.

The validator accepts hosts such as `example.com:8080`, but record_for_host extracts only URI.host (`example.com`) and compares it to the stored port-qualified string. An accepted and saved host therefore never authorizes its corresponding URLs. Normalize the stored and queried authority consistently, including a deliberate port policy.

issues.descricao: EmbeddableHost's host format validation only accepts TLDs of 2-5 letters, so admins cannot add embeddable hosts on longer TLDs like example.technology.

sugestoes.texto: When no `Clients` type resource exists, authorization throws `NullPointerException` and turns a deny into a 500. Check the fallback from `getResourceTypeResource` for null before calling `findByResource(server, resource)`.

Removing a client, role, or group with both V1 and V2 enabled crashes event dispatch with `UnsupportedOperationException` because `management()` returns V2 whose `setPermissionsEnabled` throws. Gate the cleanup listener on `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` without `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2`.

A caller with only `MANAGE` on all clients fails `canView`/`canList`/`requireList` and cannot list or view clients despite having full manage rights. Check `MANAGE` in global `canView()` alongside `VIEW` for consistency with `canView(ClientScopeModel)` and `UserPermissionsV2`.

A global grant is silently ignored once any per-client resource exists, denying legitimate admins in `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)`. Check the per-client resource from `findByName` and then the all-clients type resource from `getResourceTypeResource` so either grant succeeds.

Listing cost grows linearly with realm client count because each resource triggers a separate store lookup and policy evaluation in `getClientsWithPermission` via `findByType`. Filter candidates by scope-associated policies before full evaluation or paginate the scan.

issues.descricao: Claims the removal-cleanup listener is guarded by the V1 fine-grained flag, so client/role/group permissions are orphaned when V1 is disabled or only V2 is enabled.
issues.textoGolden: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

comentarios.texto: The cleanup is now entirely wrapped in Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ), so when the feature is disabled the pre-existing removal cleanup (roles/clients/groups .setPermissionsEnabled(..., false)) no longer runs. Realms using the non-V2 permission model will keep orphaned authorization resources/permissions after a client, role or group is removed. The gate should preserve the old behavior when the feature is off (run for V1), or the V1 cleanup must be performed elsewhere.

issues.descricao: getClientsWithPermission in ClientPermissionsV2 only finds the type-level 'Clients' resource and returns its name, never actual client ids, so callers that resolve the returned values as client ids get wrong results or null clients.
issues.textoGolden: In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

issues.descricao: Claims getResourceTypeResource can return null in ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, causing a NullPointerException in findByResource.
issues.textoGolden: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.

issues.descricao: ClientPermissionsV2 has an unused private getEvaluationContext method.
issues.textoGolden: Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called

comentarios.texto: Dead computation: `getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken)` is private and has no caller anywhere in the class. Its only possible consumer in the V1 class, `canExchangeTo`, was overridden to throw UnsupportedOperationException (line 148-150). The EvaluationContext and its overridden getBaseAttributes are built and then never used — remove the method (or wire it into canExchangeTo if token-exchange is meant to be supported).

issues.descricao: The Javadoc of the void requireView() and requireViewClientScopes() methods says they return true instead of documenting that they throw ForbiddenException.

comentarios.texto: The Javadoc for `void requireView()` says "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canView()} returns {@code true}", but requireView() is void and throws ForbiddenException rather than returning a value. It is a copy-paste of the canView() doc and should read "Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canView()} returns {@code false}", matching the sibling require* methods (requireListClientScopes, requireConfigure, etc.).

The Javadoc for `void requireViewClientScopes()` says "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canViewClientScopes()} returns {@code true}", but the method is void and throws ForbiddenException. The doc describes a boolean return the method never produces; it should state that it throws ForbiddenException if canViewClientScopes() returns false, consistent with the other require* methods.

Declaration does not match the method it documents: the javadoc for `requireView()` ('Returns {@code true} if {@link #canView()} returns {@code true}.') and for `requireViewClientScopes()` ('Returns {@code true} if {@link #canViewClientScopes()} returns {@code true}.') describes a boolean-returning accessor, but both methods are declared `void` and are the require* counterparts that throw ForbiddenException (as documented for requireManage/requireConfigure above). The text was copy-pasted from the corresponding can* methods; it should state that the method throws when canView()/canViewClientScopes() is false.

issues.descricao: ClientPermissionsV2.canView() ignores a global MANAGE permission, so admins with only global manage take the unpaginated, per-client evaluated listing path.

comentarios.texto: canView() does not recognize an all-clients MANAGE permission even though canView(client) grants viewing through canConfigure(client) and canManage(client). For an administrator with global MANAGE but no VIEW, ClientsResource.getClients selects an unpaginated realm-wide client stream and evaluates authorization for clients before applying pagination, instead of fetching the requested database page. Include the global MANAGE permission in the global viewing capability while preserving client-specific denial semantics.

issues.descricao: canView(client) short-circuits on the global all-clients VIEW permission, so a client-specific permission denying an admin is never evaluated and the client is still viewable.

comentarios.texto: The global VIEW check returns true before evaluating client-specific VIEW permissions, bypassing a negative permission on an individual client. An administrator granted VIEW on all clients can therefore read a client explicitly excluded by a client-specific denial; ClientsResource.getClients also bypasses per-client checks when this evaluator's parameterless canView() returns true. Evaluate the specific client resource before falling back to the all-clients permission, and ensure listing does not use a global grant to skip specific denials.

Do not short-circuit resource-specific view evaluation on the global fine-grained VIEW grant. With an all-clients VIEW permission allowing an administrator and a client-specific VIEW permission denying that administrator, canView() returns true here and the specific client permission is never evaluated. This differs from the specific-over-global override behavior exercised for users in this PR and exposes the denied client's representation. Keep the administrative-role bypass separate from fine-grained grants and evaluate the client's resource before falling back to the all-clients resource; also ensure the global view result used by client listing cannot bypass those overrides.

issues.descricao: The negative check for removing a default client scope expects ForbiddenException, but it can come from the preceding getDefaultClientScopes() call, so the test passes even without a permission check on removal.

comentarios.texto: The expected ForbiddenException can come from getDefaultClientScopes(), before removeDefaultClientScope() is invoked. With no permission granted, the initial read is forbidden, so this test still passes if removal's manage-permission check is removed entirely; the later granted removal also succeeds in that broken implementation. Obtain the scope ID using the privileged realm client outside this try block, then invoke only removeDefaultClientScope() through the restricted client and assert that it is forbidden.

issues.descricao: ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException, but AbstractTokenExchangeProvider still calls clients().canExchangeTo for client-to-client exchange, so with token exchange and FGAP V2 enabled the request fails with a server error instead of a permission decision.

sugestoes.texto: `Upload.create_for` handles SVG via `Nokogiri` without rasterizing, so rewriting it with `convert -resize 80%>` corrupts the vector. Exclude `/\.svg$/i` from the auto-downsize branch guarded by `FileHelper.is_image?`.

Ruby has no overloading, so only the 3-positional version survives and the existing `ResizeEmoji` call with `downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)` raises `ArgumentError`. Keep one flexible definition that accepts both forms or update `resize_emoji.rb` to pass `"100x100"`.

This breaks the admin contract in both directions, blocking files the server allows while permitting 10MB attachments the server rejects with a misleading error. Restore the per-type `SiteSettings` lookup for `max_image/attachment_size_kb` in `validateUploadedFile` and the 413 handler.

Each `convert` plus `ImageOptim` pass is CPU-heavy and runs synchronously, so up to 5 sequential passes on files up to 10MB stall workers and enable CPU exhaustion. Check the return value from `OptimizedImage.downsize` and reject or defer after one failed attempt.

An authenticated attacker controls the fetch target, so the larger fixed cap increases SSRF bandwidth and internal-fetch abuse beyond configured policy. Restore the `SiteSetting`-derived cap from `max_image_size_kb` for `FileHelper.download` of the API-supplied `url`.

issues.descricao: downsize is defined twice in OptimizedImage; the new (from, to, dimensions, opts) version overrides the (max_width, max_height) one, so existing callers such as ResizeEmoji that pass width and height now raise ArgumentError.
issues.textoGolden: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: A second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` is defined that overrides the existing `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at lines 145-147. WHY: Ruby uses the last definition, so the effective downsize now only accepts 3-4 args, and the existing caller app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14 (`OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)`) passes 5 args and raises ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments, given 5, expected 3..4), breaking emoji resizing. HOW: Remove the duplicate; keep a single downsize method whose signature matches all callers (the 4-arg uploads_controller call `downsize(path, path, "80%", allow_animation: ...)` and the 5-arg ResizeEmoji call), or rename one of them.

`downsize` is defined twice: the original 5-param form `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` at lines 145-147 and the new 4-param form `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts)` at lines 149-151. Ruby keeps only the last definition, so the effective signature is now 4 params and the 5-param version is dead code. The pre-existing consumer app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14 still calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)` with 5 positional args, which now raises ArgumentError on every emoji resize. Either update that caller to the new `dimensions` form or remove the redundant override so the old signature keeps working.

`self.downsize` is defined twice in the same class scope (line 145 `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` and the new line 149 `(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`). Ruby keeps only the last definition, so the 4-argument version is dead and unreachable. The existing caller `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)` in app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14 passes 5 arguments and will now raise ArgumentError (expected 3..4). Remove the duplicate definition (keep only the `dimensions`-based one, or convert resize_emoji's call), otherwise emoji resizing breaks.

issues.descricao: The client-side upload size check hardcodes 10 MB instead of the per-type max_<type>_size_kb setting, so attachment limits diverge from the server: larger allowed attachments are blocked and smaller limits are only enforced server-side.
issues.textoGolden: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).

comentarios.texto: Hardcoded max size literal 10 * 1024 replaces site-setting-derived max size. Behavioral concern outside assigned class.

The fixed 10 MB client limit is applied to attachments as well as images, replacing max_attachment_size_kb. Sites configured to allow attachments larger than 10 MB can no longer upload those valid files through the composer, although UploadValidator still permits them. Apply the new input ceiling only to images and retain the configured attachment limit.

WHAT: Client check hardcodes maxSizeKB to 10*1024 instead of Discourse.SiteSettings['max_'+type+'_size_kb'], losing image vs attachment distinction. WHY: Sites with smaller max_attachment_size_kb pass client validation then fail server-side, and sites with limits >10MB incorrectly block valid uploads with wrong max_size_kb message. HOW: Restore per-type SiteSetting lookup (keep 10MB only as image downsize ceiling).

issues.descricao: The upload downsizing passes a percentage ('80%') as dimensions, but for animated GIFs the gifsicle path uses --resize-fit, which expects WxH geometry, so downsizing silently fails.
issues.textoGolden: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.

comentarios.texto: The controller passes the percentage string `"80%"` as the dimensions argument to `OptimizedImage.downsize`, but the consumer requires explicit `WxH` geometry: the code this PR deleted built exactly `"#{width}x#{height}"`, and the animated path runs `gifsicle --resize-fit #{dimensions}`, which rejects a percentage. Pass an explicit size (e.g. a computed `"WxH"` from the max KB target) so the auto-downsize actually reduces the file, rather than silently no-oping and leaving oversized uploads.

Caller passes "80%" as dimensions to OptimizedImage.downsize, but the downsize/optimize instruction builders in optimized_image.rb expect explicit "WxH" geometry (interpolated as -resize #{dimensions}\>). A bare percentage does not satisfy that contract and will produce a malformed geometry. Fix the caller to supply WxH dimensions or add explicit percentage handling to the callee.

issues.descricao: Auto-downsizing passes the upload tempfile path, which lacks a .gif extension, so the animated branch is never chosen and convert keeps only the first frame, flattening oversized animated GIFs.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: The new auto-downsize call passes a tempfile path whose name has no `.GIF` extension, so `optimize` never selects the animated branch (`method_name += "_animated" if opts[:allow_animation] && from =~ /\.GIF$/i`) and uses `downsize_instructions`, which runs `convert from[0]` and keeps only the first frame. WHY: Animated GIFs larger than max_image_size_kb that are uploaded through this path have their animation flattened to a single frame even though SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails is enabled. HOW: Detect the image type from the original filename/content-type rather than the tempfile path (or pass a flag) so the gifsicle animated downsize path is used for GIF inputs.

Passing the multipart tempfile path to downsize prevents animation detection when that path does not end in .gif, even when allow_animated_thumbnails is enabled. OptimizedImage.optimize checks the path suffix and otherwise uses convert with input[0], so oversized animated GIF uploads are permanently flattened to their first frame. Preserve the original image extension in the processing path or pass the image format explicitly to select animated processing.

issues.descricao: The comment promises images are reduced to the allowed size, but the loop only tries five 80% reductions with no guarantee of reaching the limit.

comentarios.texto: The comment says large images are "automatically reduced to allowed size", but the loop only resizes by 80% up to 5 attempts (≈0.33× of the original in the best case) and then stops without any check that the result actually meets `max_image_size_kb`. The prose promises a guarantee the code does not provide; either make the loop actually converge to the allowed size or reword the comment to state that the image is only attempted to be reduced.

issues.descricao: The downsize retry loop ignores the false return of a failed conversion and repeats the same failing ImageMagick call up to five times.

comentarios.texto: The retry loop ignores downsize's false return value and retries failed conversions while the file remains oversized. convert_with returns false on converter failure, so an unsupported or malformed oversized image launches the same failing external conversion up to five times per upload without any changed input. Break on a failed downsize result and return an upload error rather than repeating the conversion.

WHAT: Downsize loop ignores OptimizedImage.downsize return value and retries up to 5 times unconditionally while checking tempfile.size. WHY: Failed converts (e.g. SVG, invalid 80%> geometry, corrupt image) burn 5 ImageMagick runs then Upload.create_for still runs with oversized/unmodified file and fails validation, wasting CPU and breaking the feature. HOW: Break on false return and handle failure.

issues.descricao: Claims up to five synchronous ImageMagick runs per oversized upload block request threads and enable DoS.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: Up to 5 synchronous OptimizedImage.downsize + ImageOptim convert runs execute inline in create_upload request cycle for every oversized image. WHY: Blocks the Rails request thread with CPU-intensive shell-outs per upload, enabling easy request-thread exhaustion/DoS with large images. HOW: Move downsizing to background job or enforce single-pass/timeout.

issues.descricao: Claims the downsize loop checking tempfile.size may never terminate because of a stale cached size, causing infinite loops.
issues.textoGolden: The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

issues.descricao: The 413 upload error message states a hard-coded 10 MB maximum that may not match the limit the server or web server actually enforces.

The upload tempfile path, which for API URL uploads embeds the request-controlled type param, is now passed to OptimizedImage.downsize and run unescaped in a shell via backticks, allowing command injection through type.

sugestoes.texto: Clicking Silence sets drawer state but renders nothing, leaving the action broken for ruler-free rules. Gate `canSilence`/`handleSilence` on `rulerRule` presence until `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` supports `promRule`, or add a `promRule`-backed drawer.

In the ruler-free list view `rulerRule` is undefined, so Pause and Delete never appear despite `canPause`/`canDelete` being allowed. Check `promRule` via `prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule` alongside `rulerRule` when gating the menu items.
Missing keys trigger React reconciliation warnings and state/identity mismatches across paginated filter results. Pass `key={key}` to `GrafanaRuleListItem` to match the sibling branches.

Datasource rules show Duplicate to users with only Grafana create permission because `skipToken` abilities returning `Duplicate` are OR-ed into `canDuplicate`. Restrict `duplicateSupported` by rule type with `isPluginProvided` so `hasGrafanaCreate` does not grant it for cloud rules.

Mimir federated rules become editable, removable, and pausable in the UI when they must stay immutable. Thread federated-group info through `groupIdentifier` instead of hardcoding `isFederated` to `false` in `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`.

issues.descricao: The pause menu item is still gated on a Grafana ruler rule, but the list view now passes only the Prometheus rule, so Pause/Resume disappears for list-view rules even when the user may pause them.

comentarios.texto: The new Prometheus-based pause ability cannot display Pause or Resume for list-view rules because the menu still requires rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) before rendering MenuItemPauseRule. GrafanaRuleListItem now supplies only promRule, so these actions disappear even for editable rules. Adapt the pause menu item to accept the Grafana identifier and Prometheus pause state, or load the ruler rule on demand.

issues.descricao: The Delete menu item still requires a ruler rule, which list-view Grafana rules no longer provide, so users with delete permission lose the Delete action.

comentarios.texto: The new Prometheus-based delete ability is still gated by `canDelete && rulerRule` when rendering the Delete item. Both Grafana list-view paths now omit rulerRule, so users with delete permission lose the Delete action entirely. Render deletion using the available identifier and group identifier instead of requiring the ruler DTO, adapting the callback contract accordingly.

issues.descricao: When the Grafana prom-rule branch is skipped (datasource rules), useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined) still reports Duplicate as supported and allowed by Grafana create permission, and AlertRuleMenu ORs it with the ruler ability, so Duplicate appears on cloud rules even when the ruler check denies it.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: canDuplicate ORs ruler ability with grafana ability where grafana path is skipToken=>undefined for cloud rules, and useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined) returns Duplicate=[true,true] whenever the user has global Grafana create permission. WHY: Any user with Grafana rule-create gets Duplicate menu item on cloud/Mimir rules even when ruler abilities deny it — incorrect authorization gating. HOW: Return NotSupported for all abilities when rule is skipToken/undefined, or gate grafana branch on prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule) before ORing.

useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities returns AlwaysSupported for Duplicate when rule is undefined (skipToken): loading is false from the !rule early-return, so MaybeSupported=true and duplicateSupported=true. ORed in AlertRuleMenu/RuleActionsButtons this leaks Grafana create permission into non-Grafana rules. Gate MaybeSupported/duplicateSupported on rule existence (e.g. NotSupported when !rule).

useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities must return NotSupported for all actions when rule is undefined (skipToken). Currently MaybeSupported falls back to AlwaysSupported when !loading, so Duplicate=[true, global-create] is true for a cloud rule passed as skipToken, and AlertRuleMenu/RuleActionsButtons OR-logic then incorrectly enables Duplicate (and Explore). Guard with if (!rule) return all-NotSupported abilities or make MaybeSupported require rule.

issues.descricao: The refactor of useAllAlertRuleAbilities into useAllRulerRuleAbilities drops the isFederatedRuleGroup check (isFederated is hardcoded false), so federated Mimir rules are reported as editable and deletable.

comentarios.texto: useAllAlertRuleAbilities now delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities, which hardcodes isFederated = false. The previous isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) check is gone, so federated Mimir rules are no longer treated as immutable and can show edit and delete abilities. Keep the federation check in this wrapper, or pass the federation state into the shared hook.

Delegating useAllAlertRuleAbilities to useAllRulerRuleAbilities discards the group's federation status and replaces the previous isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) check with a constant false. Legacy RuleActionsButtons consequently enables editing rules in groups with source_tenants, although these groups were explicitly immutable before this change. Preserve the CombinedRule federation check in the wrapper or pass federation status into the delegated ability calculation.

Preserve the federated-group immutability check when delegating this CombinedRule hook. Previously useAllAlertRuleAbilities inspected rule.group with isFederatedRuleGroup and disabled modification/removal for federated rules. The replacement delegates to a hook that hardcodes isFederated=false and receives no group information. Existing useAlertRuleAbility/useAlertRuleAbilities consumers therefore now receive supported update/delete abilities for federated rules when datasource permissions allow them, exposing operations that the previous contract explicitly prohibited. Pass the federation state through or retain that restriction in this wrapper.

issues.descricao: The Grafana prom-rule abilities gate Pause, Restore, Export and DeletePermanently on alertingRule(rule) while the comment claims it checks Grafana-managed rules, so Grafana recording rules lose these actions in the list view.

comentarios.texto: The comment says all GrafanaPromRuleDTO rules are Grafana-managed, but the variable it describes is `isAlertingRule`. That variable is true only for alerting rules and false for Grafana recording rules. Fix the comment, or rename the variable, so it says the check is for alerting rules. As written, readers will expect Pause, Export and Silence to be enabled for recording rules.

The comment says all GrafanaPromRuleDTO rules are Grafana-managed, but the check used is alertingRule(rule), which is false for recording rules. Pause, Restore, ModifyExport and DeletePermanently are therefore wrongly disabled for Grafana recording rules, where the old isGrafanaManagedAlertRule check allowed them. Use prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(rule) for these abilities, and keep alertingRule only for Silence.

issues.descricao: The comment claims GrafanaPromRuleDTO abilities have no loading state, but the next line makes support depend on the folder loading flag.

comentarios.texto: The comment says there is no loading state, but the next line is `loading ? NotSupported : AlwaysSupported`. `loading` comes from the folder fetch. Update the comment to say that support depends on the folder loading state.

issues.descricao: The Grafana branch of the filtered rule list renders GrafanaRuleListItem without a key prop, so React reconciles the streaming list by index and warns about missing keys.
issues.textoGolden: The rendered GrafanaRuleListItem is missing the required key prop for React list items. This can cause rendering issues when the list order changes.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: The grafana branch of the filtered list renders <GrafanaRuleListItem .../> without a `key` prop, dropping the `key={key}` that the replaced <GrafanaRuleLoader key={key} .../> had. WHY: `rules.map` renders a dynamic list keyed by getRuleKey/hashRule; without a key React logs duplicate-key warnings and reconciles rows by index, so as the async rule stream updates/reorders the wrong rule row can be reused/mutated (stale state, swapped actions). It finds the button by name 'More', so the aria-label and text assertions are tautological. It would pass even if the menu had no actions or the abilities were broken. Click the button and assert the expected menu items, or rename the test to match what it checks.

Test named 'should render More button with action menu options' never opens the menu nor asserts menu items — it only checks More button presence/aria/text. Click More and assert expected menuitems (or rename to 'should render More button') so it fails if menu actions break.

Clicking Silence only updates showSilenceDrawer and displays nothing because rule is undefined.
